scopeReview: PSO-6.A.1–2: urban site/situation and influences from transport, communication, population, migration, development and policy. Distinguishes urban headcount growth, statistical reclassification and increasing urban share.6.2 megacity/suburban forms reserved for the next topic.
varietyReview: Four meaningful stimuli:original coastal-site map, growth ledger including reclassification, urban/rural count bars and changed hub-access network. Checks locate supplied site data, balance distinct components, recompute shares and compare access before/after. Applied historical/policy/evidence cases complete eleven.
repetitionReview: Site characteristics, reclassification, changing national shares and relative travel access require distinct operations. Population ledger includes a new nonmigration classification component; no old numerical-only clone. Original fictional cities and data, varied keys, complete explanations; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official scope checked directly. All maps, populations and urban scenarios original/hypothetical; no real first-city date, current ranking, forecast or resource added. No independent human review claimed.

questions.correctOption: The inlet and near-level ground at the settlement itself.
questions.independentReview: Checked P lies on the land side beside the supplied inlet at the river mouth; depth/shelter come from explicit hypothetical notes, not inferred from an outline. Distinguished local characteristics from regional access without asserting deterministic city growth.

Independently balanced births−deaths=2000, arrivals−departures=4000, reclassified=2000, total8000. Reclassification explicitly excludes any duplication with births/migration and concerns statistical urban growth, unlike simply repeating an earlier natural-growth item.

questions.correctOption: Urban population rises, but its share falls from 50% to 40% because rural population grows faster.
questions.independentReview: Independently summed200→300 thousand and ratios100/200=.5,120/300=.4; urban count100→120, rural100→180. Definitions constant to exclude reclassification as an alternative explanation.

questions.correctOption: P becomes faster to reach the hub than Q, despite no change in P’s physical site.
questions.independentReview: Independently compared60>30 initially and20<30 afterward. P improves40 minutes, Q0. Fixed node positions and no physical-site change explicitly supplied; no actual causal city-growth estimate.

questions.correctOption: Food beyond producers’ immediate needs can support people specializing in nonfarm work, provided systems of exchange and distribution exist.
questions.independentReview: Checked a conditional origin mechanism rather than a single-cause history of all cities. No exact date, first-city ranking or universal development sequence asserted.

questions.correctOption: Policy can concentrate employment and access, potentially attracting residents and businesses alongside other conditions.
questions.independentReview: Aligned PSO-6.A.2 government-policy influence without an actual capital-city case or guaranteed growth claim.

questions.correctOption: Its situation within transport networks changed while many site characteristics stayed the same.
questions.independentReview: Distinct from the travel-time diagram: this concerns historical functional decline after network bypass rather than a shorter trip to one hub. Fictional example, no disputed real port history.

questions.correctOption: Job opportunities can attract migration while urban outcomes still depend on labor demand, housing and other constraints.
questions.independentReview: Separated motivation from guaranteed outcomes without stereotyping rural migrants or assigning a real city’s labor conditions.

questions.correctOption: All cities must become obsolete because digital communication removes every advantage of concentration.
questions.independentReview: No current technology adoption statistic or forecast claimed. Evaluated model scope and differing functions rather than asserting digital tools always decentralize all work.

questions.correctOption: Matched information on migration, natural increase, employment, transport investment and policy over the same period.
questions.independentReview: Evidence-selection question, not a promise that correlation isolates every causal contribution. Scope consistent with PSO-6.A.1–2.

questions.correctOption: Physical conditions create constraints and opportunities that technology and policy can modify, while costs and residual risks remain.
questions.independentReview: A conceptual hypothetical, not engineering advice or a real flood forecast. Site constraints acknowledged without claiming they alone determine a city’s existence or growth.
